evals.prompt: Add some nice animations to our app: the command palette (Cmd+K), the settings modal, the dropdown menus, and toasts. Make it feel premium.
evals.expected_output: Applies the frequency gate: the Cmd+K palette gets no open/close animation; modal, dropdowns and toasts get short ease-out transitions with exact curves and durations, origin-aware dropdowns, toasts via transitions, and a reduced-motion variant for each.
expectations: The command palette opened via keyboard shortcut is left un-animated (or explicitly instant)
Uses an ease-out cubic-bezier for entrances and does not use ease-in for any entrance
All UI durations are at or under 300 ms (drawers/sheets excepted)
No entrance starts from scale(0); starts around 0.95 or higher
Dropdown transform-origin is set to the trigger while the modal stays centered
Includes a prefers-reduced-motion variant that keeps opacity and removes movement, without a global 0.01ms kill switch
Animates only transform and opacity and does not use transition: all

evals.prompt: Build a mobile bottom sheet in React that users can drag down to dismiss. Right now it only closes if you drag it more than half way and it feels dead.
evals.expected_output: Implements velocity-based dismissal alongside the distance threshold, pointer capture, 1:1 tracking with grab offset, rubber-banding above the top, spring with velocity handoff on release, cancel handling, and a non-drag close control.
expectations: Dismisses on release velocity (around 0.11 px/ms) as well as distance
Uses setPointerCapture (or the library equivalent) once dragging starts
Applies rubber-band resistance past the boundary instead of a hard clamp
Hands release velocity to a spring or uses an iOS-like drawer curve
Handles pointercancel or lost capture so state resets
Provides a non-drag way to close (button or Escape) for WCAG 2.5.7

evals.prompt: Our landing page scroll animations are janky on Android phones. We use a scroll event listener that sets opacity and top on each section.
evals.expected_output: Replaces scroll listeners with scroll-driven animations behind @supports (or IntersectionObserver), switches from top to transform, keeps content visible by default, disables under reduced motion, and notes Firefox lacks scroll-driven animations as of 2026-09.
expectations: Removes the scroll event listener as the animation driver
Animates translate/transform and opacity instead of top
Wraps animation-timeline usage in @supports and a reduced-motion query
States that scroll-driven animations are not Baseline (missing in Firefox stable) and are progressive enhancement
Content is visible without the animation running

evals.prompt: Should the success message after saving a form be a toast or shown inline next to the Save button?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a feedback-pattern choice, not a motion question. Answers briefly (inline feedback near the trigger for a single form save) or routes to interaction-design, without producing a motion spec.
expectations: Does not produce easing curves, durations, or spring parameters as the main answer
Addresses the toast-versus-inline pattern decision or points to interaction-design
